task1.title: Exchange students between Europe and Australia, 2007 and 2009
task1.prompt: The two tables below show the number of exchange students who studied at universities in Europe and Australia in 2007 and 2009.

chartDesc.title: Exchange student from universities in Europe to Australia / Exchange student from Australia universities to universities in Europe
chartDesc.overview: Overall, the total number of exchange students going from European universities to Australia increased noticeably between 2007 and 2009, whereas the total number of Australian students going to Europe remained unchanged. Germany showed the biggest increase in students going to Australia, while France hosted the highest number of Australian exchange students by 2009.
keyFeatures: The total number of exchange students from Europe to Australia grew from 189 in 2007 to 226 in 2009, largely due to a significant rise in German students (27 to 62).
The total number of Australian exchange students heading to Europe remained stable at exactly 152 in both 2007 and 2009.
France provided the highest number of exchange students to Australia in 2007 (61) and received the highest number of Australian students in 2009 (58).
Student exchanges involving the United Kingdom decreased in both directions (31 to 26 to Australia; 32 to 23 to Europe).

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The two tables compare how many exchange students travelled between universities in five European countries and Australia in 2007 and 2009, in each direction.

Overall, considerably more students moved from Europe to Australia than in the opposite direction, and this flow grew over the period while the Australian outflow remained exactly the same in total. The most dramatic individual changes were the German surge towards Australia and the French rise in the reverse flow.

European arrivals in Australia increased from 189 to 226. France sent the most students in 2007, at 61, and its figure was almost unchanged at 60 in 2009, but Germany more than doubled its numbers, from 27 to 62, to become the largest source. Sweden's total also grew, from 34 to 42, whereas the United Kingdom's fell to 26 and the Netherlands held steady at 36.

Traffic the other way totalled 152 students in both years, but its composition shifted markedly. The number of Australians choosing France jumped from 37 to 58, making it comfortably the most popular destination, and Germany also rose from 18 to 26. In contrast, the figures for Sweden, the UK and especially the Netherlands — down from 32 to 18 — all declined.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Ikkita jadval 2007 va 2009-yillarda besh Yevropa mamlakati universitetlari bilan Avstraliya o'rtasida har ikki yo'nalishda qancha almashinuv talabasi qatnaganini solishtiradi.

Umuman olganda, Yevropadan Avstraliyaga teskari yo'nalishdagidan ancha ko'p talaba borgan va bu oqim davr mobaynida o'sgan, Avstraliyadan chiquvchi oqim esa jami hisobda aynan bir xilligicha qolgan. Eng keskin alohida o'zgarishlar — Germaniyaning Avstraliya tomon sakrashi va qarama-qarshi oqimdagi Fransiyaning o'sishi bo'ldi.

Avstraliyaga kelgan yevropaliklar soni 189 dan 226 ga ko'paydi. 2007-yilda eng ko'p talabani — 61 nafar — Fransiya yuborgan va uning ko'rsatkichi 2009-yilda 60 bilan deyarli o'zgarmadi, biroq Germaniya o'z sonini 27 dan 62 ga yetkazib ikki baravardan ko'proq oshirdi va eng yirik manbaga aylandi. Shvetsiya ham 34 dan 42 ga o'sdi, Buyuk Britaniya esa 26 ga tushdi, Niderlandiya 36 da barqaror qoldi.

Teskari yo'nalishdagi qatnov har ikki yilda ham jami 152 talabani tashkil etdi, ammo uning tarkibi sezilarli o'zgardi. Fransiyani tanlagan avstraliyaliklar soni 37 dan 58 ga sakrab, uni ishonchli farq bilan eng ommabop manzilga aylantirdi, Germaniya ham 18 dan 26 ga ko'tarildi. Bundan farqli o'laroq, Shvetsiya, Buyuk Britaniya va ayniqsa Niderlandiya — 32 dan 18 ga tushgan — ko'rsatkichlari pasaydi.

task2.title: Economic growth: end to poverty or threat to the environment?
task2.prompt: Some people say that economic growth is the only way to end hunger and poverty, while others say that economic growth is damaging the environment and therefore must be stopped. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
How to reconcile prosperity with a habitable planet is one of the defining debates of our time. Some insist that only economic growth can eradicate hunger and poverty, while others want growth halted to save the environment. I believe both positions are too extreme, and that the answer lies in changing the nature of growth rather than stopping it.

The first view rests on solid evidence. Growth in countries such as China and Vietnam has lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty within a generation, funding the food, jobs, hospitals and schools that aid alone could never provide. For a poor country, telling its citizens to stop growing amounts to freezing them in deprivation, which is why no serious anti-poverty strategy ignores the economy.

Yet the environmental objection is equally real. Growth as currently pursued burns fossil fuels, clears forests and depletes fisheries and soil; climate change, moreover, hits the poorest hardest, so unchecked growth can undermine the very progress it finances. What this proves, however, is not that growth must be stopped, but that it must be decoupled from environmental damage. Renewable energy, green taxes, strict conservation laws and investment in clean technology allow economies to expand while their carbon footprint shrinks, as several European countries have already demonstrated.

In conclusion, I side with neither camp entirely: growth remains indispensable for ending poverty, but only sustainable, well-regulated growth deserves support. The real choice is not between prosperity and the planet — it is between reckless growth and responsible growth.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Farovonlikni yashash mumkin bo'lgan sayyora bilan qanday uyg'unlashtirish — davrimizning eng muhim bahslaridan biri. Ba'zilar ochlik va qashshoqlikni faqat iqtisodiy o'sish tag-tomiri bilan yo'q qila olishini ta'kidlasa, boshqalar atrof-muhitni asrash uchun o'sishni to'xtatishni istaydi. Menimcha, har ikkala pozitsiya ham haddan tashqari keskin va yechim o'sishni to'xtatishda emas, uning tabiatini o'zgartirishdadir.

Birinchi qarash mustahkam dalillarga tayanadi. Xitoy va Vetnam kabi mamlakatlardagi o'sish bir avlod ichida yuzlab million odamni qashshoqlikdan olib chiqdi va yordamning o'zi hech qachon ta'minlay olmaydigan oziq-ovqat, ish o'rinlari, kasalxona va maktablarni moliyalashtirdi. Kambag'al mamlakat uchun fuqarolariga o'sishni to'xtating deyish ularni muhtojlikda muzlatib qo'yish bilan barobar — shuning uchun birorta jiddiy qashshoqlikka qarshi strategiya iqtisodiyotni e'tibordan chetda qoldirmaydi.

Biroq ekologik e'tiroz ham xuddi shunday real. Hozirgi ko'rinishdagi o'sish qazilma yoqilg'ini yoqadi, o'rmonlarni kesadi, baliq zaxiralari va tuproqni kamaytirib boradi; iqlim o'zgarishi esa eng kambag'allarga eng qattiq zarba beradi, shu bois nazoratsiz o'sish o'zi moliyalashtirgan taraqqiyotni izdan chiqarishi mumkin. Ammo bu o'sishni to'xtatish kerakligini emas, uni ekologik zarardan ajratish zarurligini isbotlaydi. Qayta tiklanadigan energiya, yashil soliqlar, qat'iy muhofaza qonunlari va toza texnologiyalarga sarmoya iqtisodiyotlarga uglerod iziga qisqargan holda kengayish imkonini beradi — buni bir qancha Yevropa mamlakatlari allaqachon ko'rsatdi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, men ikkala lagerga ham to'liq qo'shilmayman: o'sish qashshoqlikni tugatish uchun muqobilsiz bo'lib qolaveradi, biroq faqat barqaror, yaxshi tartibga solingan o'sishgina qo'llab-quvvatlashga loyiq. Haqiqiy tanlov farovonlik bilan sayyora o'rtasida emas — mas'uliyatsiz o'sish bilan mas'uliyatli o'sish o'rtasidadir.
